question: Can a LightGBM model that uses network context (neighbouring-link flows and node activity) beat a standard per-link linear trend extrapolation at predicting next-period cattle movement counts between premises?
method: Seeded synthetic premises-movement simulation (gravity base rate, per-link trends, AR(1) node shocks); time-ordered split; CV tuning on training months; test set used once per model; seeds 42, 43, 44.

dataset.name: Simulated premises-to-premises cattle movement network (generated in analysis.py)

metric_name: MAE on raw next-month link counts
baseline: Per-link linear trend fitted by OLS to the last 6 monthly counts, extrapolated one month ahead and clipped at zero.
improved: LightGBM regressor on log1p counts using lagged counts, rolling means, and network features from the previous month (out/in degree and neighbouring-link flows at source and destination premises); hyper-parameters chosen by time-ordered CV on training data.
notes: Synthetic data stand in for the paper's Great Britain cattle movement records, which are not publicly downloadable; results do not transfer to real data. The baseline is a plain trend tracker, not the paper's predictive trend mining framework. Std is the population std (ddof=0) over 3 simulation seeds. Secondary metrics: top-decile hit rate (overlap of top-10% predicted and actual links) and F1 on active links (count>0) with a 0.5 threshold on predictions. The test set was used once per model.
